candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: assess age-related risks, provide preventive-health education, promote safe physical activity and reduce modifiable risks for injury and loss of function.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Preventive screening and modification of fall-related risk factors
candidate.educational_objective: Use a proactive multifactorial fall-prevention plan for older adults that addresses medications, vision, footwear, strength/balance, and environmental hazards rather than restricting activity or waiting for a first fall.

options.A: Review medications that may cause dizziness or drowsiness, keep vision correction current, use well-fitting nonslip footwear, improve strength and balance, and remove home tripping hazards or add safety supports as needed.
options.B: Avoid nearly all physical activity because reducing movement is the most effective way to prevent falls in older adults.
options.C: Wait until a first fall occurs before addressing medications, vision, footwear, balance, or home hazards because prevention is not useful beforehand.
options.D: Focus only on one home modification because medication effects, vision, strength, balance, and footwear have little relationship to fall risk.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current CDC STEADI resources use a multifactorial approach to older-adult fall prevention. Modifiable factors include medications that cause dizziness, sedation or balance problems; vision impairment; unsafe footwear; weakness or poor balance; and environmental hazards such as loose rugs, inadequate lighting, missing grab bars or stair rails. Strength and balance activity is encouraged rather than blanket activity restriction. B can worsen deconditioning and does not reflect STEADI prevention. C is incorrect because fall-risk screening and prevention are proactive. D ignores multiple established modifiable risks. The final item tests a practical prevention plan rather than a memorized list and remains distinct from postoperative fall-prevention questions in this batch.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC sources directly support multifactorial fall prevention addressing medications, vision, footwear, physical function and home hazards before a fall occurs.
candidate.source_document_title: STEADI - Older Adult Fall Prevention; Pharmacy Care (STEADI-Rx); About Vision Impairment and Falls Among Older Adults; Preventing Falls and Hip Fractures
candidate.source_locator: CDC STEADI → clinical resources and patient resources: screen and intervene on modifiable fall risks. STEADI-Rx: medication review for medicines causing drowsiness, loss of balance, vision changes or slower reactions. CDC Vision and Falls: strength/balance exercise, sturdy nonslip footwear, current eye exams and medication review. CDC fall-prevention guidance: remove trip hazards, improve lighting, install grab bars and stair railings.
